notes:
Xcode restructure plus two transport-timing fixes. RESTRUCTURE: all 67 Swift files moved from ios/ root into the synchronized ios/Sorriva/ folder; 268 lines removed from project.pbxproj, exactly the predicted 67 x 4 (file reference, build file, group child, sources entry), leaving 5 explicit references for the app product and packages. Verified each file compiles exactly once — had the old references survived alongside the synchronized folder, everything would have built twice and failed on duplicate symbols. Git recorded all 67 as renames so history is preserved, and Tom confirmed the build in Xcode and on device. A new .swift file dropped into ios/Sorriva/ is now in the build with no project edit — the manual step that broke the build when RadioServiceAdapter.swift was added. server/swift-config.json deleted: a retired packaging file list, no consumers, and its contents wrong twice over.

PHANTOM PAUSE AFTER TRANSFERS, reported by Tom and confirmed from his log. A transfer measured 11:42:34.488 -> 11:42:39.737, i.e. 5.25s, against a 5s declarationGrace — so the transport intent, declared at the START of transferPlayback, had already expired a quarter-second BEFORE Play was sent, and the zone rendered whatever Sonos reported mid-handover. It surfaced only now because SonosZone.playingUntil used +6s and covered the gap by ~0.7s, which is precisely why steps 1-4 shipped with both mechanisms live. The same problem had already been solved once for the CONTENT declaration (touchDeclaration, with a comment explaining it); the transport equivalent was simply never added.

THEN AUDITED EVERY OTHER DECLARATION SITE rather than waiting for a soak to surface the next one, and it found one: local playback's window is consumed by queueing, which is one AddURIToQueue per track. Measured over 80 real playback starts — 10 tracks 1.29s, 15 tracks 2.99s, 100 tracks 4.70s against a 5s window. Never observed, and no album in the library approaches that, but queue management will make queue length unbounded. Both fixes re-declare when the command actually goes out, which removes the dependency on elapsed work rather than widening a constant — identical for 3 tracks or 300.

Phase E step 5 (deleting playingUntil) is now unblocked on evidence rather than elapsed time.
